meta.name: US Staffing Payroll Compliance Dataset
meta.disclaimer: Reference information compiled from official government sources. Not legal or tax advice. Check the cited source before relying on any value.

facts.value: not later than the sixth day after discharge
facts.summary: Texas: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due not later than the sixth day after discharge.
facts.evidence_quote: Sec. 61.014. (a) An employer shall pay in full an employee who is discharged from employment not later than the sixth day after the date the employee is discharged.
facts.source_title: Texas Labor Code, Chapter 61 (Payment of Wages)
facts.notes: Sec. 61.001 defines 'Day' as a calendar day.

facts.value: not later than the next regularly scheduled payday
facts.summary: Texas: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due not later than the next regularly scheduled payday.
facts.evidence_quote: Sec. 61.014. (b) An employer shall pay in full an employee who leaves employment other than by discharge not later than the next regularly scheduled payday.
facts.source_title: Texas Labor Code, Chapter 61 (Payment of Wages)

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Texas basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $7.25.
facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $7.25 The State law excludes from coverage any employment that is subject to the federal Fair Labor Standards Act. The Texas State minimum wage law does not contain current dollar minimums. Instead the State adopts the federal minimum wage rate by reference.
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.value: Employers must report new hires and rehires within 20 calendar days from the date in which the employee starts earning wages.
facts.summary: Texas new hire reporting timeframe (per OCSE): Employers must report new hires and rehires within 20 calendar days from the date in which the employee starts earning wages.
facts.evidence_quote: Reporting Timeframe: Employers must report new hires and rehires within 20 calendar days from the date in which the employee starts earning wages.
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Federal floor is 20 days; states may set shorter deadlines. Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.summary: Texas: frequencies marked in the U.S. DOL State Payday Requirements table: Bi-weekly (note 21); Semi-monthly; Monthly (note 21).
facts.source_title: State Payday Requirements (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Note 21: Texas. Each employee who is exempt from the overtime provisions of the federal Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) must be paid at least once a month; others must be paid at least twice a month. Semi-monthly pay periods must contain as nearly as possible an equal number of days. Within those limitations, an employer may designate any paydays he or she chooses. | DOL table last revised 2023-01-01; DOL says to consult the state labor office for official information. Confirm against current state law before relying on it.

facts.value: FLSA-exempt employees at least monthly; all others at least twice a month
facts.summary: Texas pay frequency rule: FLSA-exempt employees at least monthly; all others at least twice a month.
facts.evidence_quote: Sec. 61.011. (a) An employer shall pay wages to each employee who is exempt from the overtime pay provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 ... at least once a month. (b) An employer shall pay wages to an employee other than an employee covered by Subsection (a) at least twice a month.

facts.summary: Texas is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration
